<thought>To infer the circuit, I first considered the measured resistances between the three nodes N_b1, X1, and X2. These three values (5 Ω, 13.333 Ω, 18.333 Ω) form a Δ (delta) network. Converting this Δ to an equivalent Y (wye) gives three series resistors that connect each of those nodes to a common internal node. Using the delta_to_wye_transform tool provides the exact values, which can then be combined with the remaining measured resistances to obtain a simple series‑parallel topology. The resulting topology consists of five resistors (R1–R5) arranged as follows:

* R1 connects A to the internal wye node.
* R2 connects B to the internal wye node.
* R3, R4, R5 are the three wye resistors obtained from the Δ‑to‑Y conversion (connected from the internal node to N_b1, X1, and X2 respectively).

All measured node‑to‑node resistances are reproduced (within the ±0.1 Ω tolerance) by this topology, so it satisfies the problem requirements.

The final JSON describes the resistor values (rounded to three decimal places) and the connections between nodes. </thought>
